name: LT3465AES6#TRPBF
title: LT3465 / LT3465A: 1.2 MHz / 2.4 MHz boost converters for white LED strings, Schottky on chip, TSOT-23
summary: Step-up converters for a series string of up to six white LEDs from a single Li-Ion cell, with the output Schottky diode on chip. A resistor at FB sets the string current against a 200 mV reference, and CTRL shuts the part down or dims it. The LT3465 switches at 1.2 MHz and has soft-start; the LT3465A switches at 2.4 MHz, has no soft-start and accepts PWM directly on CTRL. Both clamp the output at 30 V if the string opens. LT3465AES6#TRPBF is the LT3465A, lead-free, on tape and reel.
key_figures: 2.6 mA typ not switching; 3.2 µA typ with CTRL = 0 V

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output, the cathode of the internal Schottky. Takes the output capacitor and the top of the LED string; a short trace to the output capacitor lowers EMI.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground; tie straight to the local ground plane.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback, regulated to 200 mV. Joins the bottom of the LED string to the current-setting resistor to ground; that resistor and the CTRL voltage set the LED current.

pins.name: CTRL
pins.function: Shutdown and dimming. Grounded or left open, the part is off. Above about 1.8 V the LEDs get full-scale current; below 1 V the current is reduced.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input; bypass it at the pin with a 1 µF X5R or X7R ceramic.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Collector of the internal power switch, and the inductor's end.

circuits.title: Li-Ion powered driver for four white LEDs (Figure 1)
circuits.description: A boost converter running from a 3 V to 5 V input (one Li-Ion cell) drives a series string of four white LEDs. L1 runs from the input to SW, and the built-in Schottky carries the energy to VOUT, where C2 holds the string's top. The string's bottom sits on FB with a 10 Ω resistor to ground, so the loop holds 200 mV across it: 20 mA through the LEDs. C1 bypasses the input. A voltage or logic level on CTRL shuts the part down or dims the string.

circuits.title: Li-Ion to two white LEDs
circuits.description: The same boost arrangement with two LEDs in the string and a 4 Ω sense resistor, which sets 50 mA at the 200 mV feedback level. This version uses a 1 µF output capacitor. CTRL is the enable and dimming input.

circuits.title: Li-Ion to three white LEDs
circuits.description: A three-LED string fed from 3 V to 5 V; 10 Ω at FB gives 20 mA. A 0.22 µF output capacitor and a 1 µF input capacitor complete it.

circuits.title: Li-Ion to five white LEDs
circuits.description: Five LEDs in series, 20 mA through a 10 Ω sense resistor, with 0.22 µF on the output and 1 µF on the input.

circuits.title: Li-Ion to six white LEDs
circuits.description: Six LEDs in series, 20 mA through 10 Ω, with a 0.47 µF output capacitor. The inductor is 47 µH with the 1.2 MHz LT3465 or 22 µH with the 2.4 MHz LT3465A.

parts.note: Murata LQH32CN470 for the LT3465, Murata LQH32CN220 for the LT3465A

circuits.title: Dimming control using a filtered PWM signal (Figure 6)
circuits.description: A PWM logic signal reaches CTRL through a 5 kΩ resistor, with 100 nF from CTRL to ground. The RC averages the PWM into a DC level on CTRL, which then sets the feedback reference and so the LED current. The RC corner sits below the PWM frequency, and the 5 kΩ is small beside the 50 kΩ input impedance of CTRL.

operation.text: Current-mode boost at a fixed frequency. The oscillator sets an SR latch every cycle, turning on the NPN power switch Q1. Comparator A2 sees, on its positive input, the sensed switch current summed with a stabilising ramp, and on its negative input the output of error amplifier A1; once the first exceeds the second, the latch resets and Q1 turns off. A1 amplifies the difference between FB and the 200 mV reference, so a rising A1 output delivers more current and a falling one less, holding FB at the reference. The CTRL voltage adjusts the reference. The LT3465A is the same apart from its 2.4 MHz oscillator (1.2 MHz in the LT3465).

Inside: a 1.25 V reference scaled to 200 mV, error amplifier A1 with RC/CC compensation, PWM comparator A2 summing a ramp, an SR latch and driver for switch Q1 with a 0.2 Ω current-sense resistor to GND, the Schottky from SW to VOUT, overvoltage protection on VOUT, and CTRL entering through 40 kΩ and 10 kΩ resistors.

The LT3465 drives three LEDs at 1.5 mA without skipping pulses (peak inductor current under 40 mA, discontinuous conduction). The LT3465A reaches 0.2 mA with three LEDs before skipping, using 1 kΩ from FB to GND (peak inductor current under 30 mA). Below that, pulses are skipped and some low-frequency ripple appears, but the average LED current stays regulated down to zero. In discontinuous mode SW rings once the inductor current reaches zero, from the inductor with the switch and diode capacitance; the ringing is harmless and a 300 Ω resistor across the inductor damps it at some cost in efficiency.
22 µH suits most LT3465 designs; 22 µH or 10 µH suits most LT3465A designs. The inductor needs low core loss at the switching frequency (1.2 MHz or 2.4 MHz) and low DCR.

Ceramic X5R or X7R capacitors keep their value over voltage and temperature better than Y5V or Z5U. 1 µF on the input and 0.22 µF on the output serve most designs; 0.22 µF covers 3, 4 or 5 LEDs. VIN is bypassed at the pin with 1 µF X5R or X7R. Capacitor makers named: Taiyo Yuden, Murata, Kemet.
The LT3465 ramps up on its own to limit input current at start-up; its soft-start time is 600 µs typical. The LT3465A has none.

When the supply first reaches VIN, current runs via L and the on-chip Schottky to charge the output capacitor up to VIN. The Schottky can take 1 A at most, so L and C are chosen to keep this peak below 1 A.

CTRL below 50 mV shuts the chip down; above 150 mV it runs. A floating CTRL also means shutdown. Above 1.8 V the feedback reference is 200 mV and the string runs at full current; between 200 mV and 1.5 V the reference, and so the LED current, follows CTRL. Below about 1 V the current is reduced.

A PWM signal averaged by an RC (Figure 6) acts as an adjustable DC voltage on CTRL. The RC corner frequency is set below the PWM frequency, and R1 is kept well below the 50 kΩ CTRL input impedance; 5 kΩ is the suggested value.

Without soft-start, the LT3465A can take a PWM signal straight on CTRL, switching the converter on and off. 0 % duty gives zero LED current, 100 % gives full current, and the average current rises in proportion to duty. The output capacitor charges and discharges each PWM period, which shapes the FB waveform: at low PWM frequency this takes a very small part of the period and average FB is linear in duty. Below 1 kHz the average FB against duty is nearly straight; above 10 kHz it bends strongly. A smaller output capacitor gives better linearity, and the output voltage (number of LEDs) also changes it. The PWM high level must be at least 1.8 V, or the feedback voltage drops.
If the LEDs are disconnected or fail open, VOUT is clamped at 30 V and the part switches at a very low rate to keep input current small.
With no soft-start the LT3465A's inrush reaches about 400 mA driving four LEDs. The LT3465 is the choice where inrush has to be kept low.

Switch edges are fast, so the high-frequency switching path is kept tight to limit EMI. COUT sits beside pins 1 and 2 (VOUT, GND), keeping the VOUT trace to it short. A ground plane runs under the part. The feedback resistor returns straight to GND on its own trace, shared with no other part. GND connects straight to the local ground plane. The recommended placement puts COUT and RFB on the pin 1 to 3 side, L and CIN on the pin 4 to 6 side, with the LED string beside COUT.
